start_here: Say to your AI: "Add the tool server at https://remote.example/mcp to my account." It runs tool:add-a-tool-server, hands you the sign-in page to open when the server asks for one, and finishes the add when you come back.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: the server's claim and its finished state are records the tool writes for the account itself.
instructions: 1. Have the remote MCP server's address ready (https://...); a key, if it takes one, goes in through the native protected key intake, never in the chat.
2. Say "Add the tool server at <address>"; the AI runs tool:add-a-tool-server with {server} and hands back the sign-in page to open.
3. Sign in on that page; the native callback hands the AI an opaque callback_intake handle, never the code itself.
4. The AI runs tool:add-a-tool-server again with {state, callback_intake}; the answer's state is ready when the server is added.

worked_examples.title: A server that asks for sign-in is added after the callback
worked_examples.ask: Add the tool server at https://remote.example/mcp.
worked_examples.given: From tools/ai-tool-catalog/test/tool-server-native-child.test.mjs (first test): the add answers an open address carrying a 48-character state; the finish with that state and the callback handle opaque-synthetic-callback exchanges once. A raw key in the input is refused with tool_server_native_input_refused. The state below is the one that test asserts.
worked_examples.hands_back: first run: {"open": "<the server's sign-in page>?state=<48 hex>"}; second run with {"state", "callback_intake": "opaque-synthetic-callback"}: {"state": "ready"}
